title: Erdős #871: Partitioning Additive Bases of Order 2

problemStatement.formal: ¬(∀ A : Set ℕ, IsAdditiveBasis2 A → RepTendsToInfty A → CanPartitionIntoBases A)
problemStatement.plain: Let A be an additive basis of order 2 with r_A(n) → ∞. Can A be partitioned into two disjoint additive bases of order 2? Answer: NO (Larsen 2026).
whyMatters: Resolves a conjecture of Erdős on the structure of additive bases
Identifies the critical growth threshold: r_A(n) → ∞ is insufficient, but r_A(n) > c·log(n) suffices
First Erdős problem disproved with AI assistance (Claude Opus 4.5)

proven: basis2_equiv: Two definitions of additive basis are equivalent
sumset_mono: Sumset is monotone in the base set
basis2_of_supset: Supersets of bases are bases
repTendsToInfty_implies_eventuallyGe: ∞ growth implies eventual bound for any t
repTendsToInfty_implies_basis: r_A(n) → ∞ implies A is a basis
repEventuallyGe_implies_basis: r_A(n) ≥ t ≥ 1 eventually implies basis

currentState.focus: Complete: comprehensive formalization with structural theory, blocking mechanism, and consequence theorems

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETE: 15 theorems, 4 axioms, 0 sorries. Comprehensive formalization of Erdős #871 disproof. Includes: core definitions (repFunc, sumset, IsAdditiveBasis2), structural theory (monotonicity, supset, membership), representation function analysis (tends to ∞ implies basis, eventually ≥ t implies basis), partition theory (blocking property, robust partitions), main theorem (erdos_871_disproved), and consequence theorems (growth rate dichotomy, Larsen subsumption).

insights: The problem has three layers: (1) fixed threshold → counterexample exists, (2) → ∞ → still counterexample, (3) > c·log(n) → partition exists
Blocking property is the key mechanism: for any partition B∪C=A, infinitely many n fail to be in both B+B and C+C
Larsen's result strictly strengthens Erdős-Nathanson since ∞ growth implies eventual bound for any fixed t
The representation function r_A(n) → ∞ automatically implies A is a basis (r_A(n) ≥ 1 eventually)
Disproved using AI assistance (Claude Opus 4.5) by modifying the Erdős-Nathanson 1989 construction
